decisions.statement: A route serving this answer has the wiring and no part of the answering.
The credential a caller is admitted on is handed in rather than read from here.
A site admitting on more than a secret hands in its own guard instead.
A guard handed in answers a refusal or nothing.
A refusal a guard answers is served whole rather than made again here.
The count answered is the reading carried in rather than a reading taken here.
A reading held fresh carries the moment it was taken and how fast it falls with the clock.
The readout answered for is handed in rather than named here.
The key a reading is answered under is read off the readout's own page.
The scale read is the scale the readout's page names rather than a scale named here.
A readout whose page cannot be read is answered under no key rather than under a guessed key.
The rungs and the words for an empty reading are read from the store.
A rung or a word the store withholds is left out rather than made up.
Nothing between here and the tile is allowed to keep an answer.
Nothing here names the site the answer is served from.
Nothing here names a readout.
Nothing here names a scale.
Nothing here names a group.
Nothing here decides the color a count is shown in.
Nothing here reads a person or a device.
A machine that starts again draws its tiles from the readout rows rather than blank.
The route for a single readout answers no reading for a reading never taken.
A reading is answered however old that reading is.
Whether a reading is current is whether its taker is well rather than how old it is.
A workstation that stops taking readings leaves every tile drawn rather than blank.

definition: what a route answers when a caller asks for one readout's reading
